# Checkov check IDs held at ZERO failures on infra/ (the .tf scan in security.yml).
#
# THIS FILE IS THE GATE. `GATE_CHECKOV=block` fails the job when any check listed here
# reports a failure; every other Checkov finding is published and does not block. The
# reasoning — why an enforce list rather than a suppression list — is in
# .github/scripts/checkov-enforced.sh and docs/security-baseline.md.
#
# THE CRITERION IS "PASSES TODAY", NOT "MATTERS MOST". Every ID below was measured at zero
# failures against checkov 3.3.9 on 2026-08-09 (508 passed / 373 failed overall). Turning
# them on therefore cost no remediation, and the list needs no argument about relative
# importance — an argument that would have to be re-litigated every time someone added a
# resource. A couple are merely operational rather than security-critical (CKV_AWS_216,
# CKV_AWS_305); they are here because they pass, which is the whole rule.
#
# The failing rules are NOT here, and each has a disposition in docs/security-baseline.md:
# no VPC, no CMK, no X-Ray, no WAF, and S3 versioning (deferred by decision — revisit
# before any real user data lands).
#
# TO REGENERATE after an intentional infra change:
#   checkov -d infra --framework terraform --skip-path .terraform --output json --compact \
#     --soft-fail > /tmp/ck.json
#   jq -r '(if type=="array" then .[0] else . end) |
#          ((.results.failed_checks // []) | map(.check_id) | unique) as $f |
#          ((.results.passed_checks // []) | map(.check_id) | unique)
#          | map(select(. as $c | $f | index($c) | not)) | .[]' /tmp/ck.json | sort
# Do NOT paste the output over this file unthinkingly: an ID that DISAPPEARS from it has
# started failing, and deleting the line is how a gate gets quietly turned off. Removing an
# entry is a decision that belongs in docs/security-baseline.md.
#
# Note: no --quiet above. It strips passed_checks, and the gate cannot tell "this check
# passed" from "this check never ran" without them.

# aws
CKV_AWS_41     # Ensure no hard coded AWS access key and secret key exists in provider (1)

# aws_athena_workgroup
CKV_AWS_159    # Ensure that Athena Workgroup is encrypted (1)

CKV2_AWS_72    # Ensure AWS CloudFront origin protocol policy enforces HTTPS-only (1)
CKV_AWS_216    # Ensure CloudFront distribution is enabled (1)
CKV_AWS_305    # Ensure CloudFront distribution has a default root object configured (1)
CKV_AWS_34     # Ensure CloudFront distribution ViewerProtocolPolicy is set to HTTPS (1)

CKV_AWS_111    # Ensure IAM policies does not allow write access without constraints (3)
CKV_AWS_283    # Ensure no IAM policies documents allow ALL or any AWS principal permissions to the resource (3)
CKV_AWS_356    # Ensure no IAM policies documents allow "*" as a statement's resource for restrictable actions (3)
CKV_AWS_358    # Ensure AWS GitHub Actions OIDC authorization policies only allow safe claims and claim order (3)
